newsitem.title: USA: Fla. oversight board sets Jan 3 deadline for Miami.
newsitem.headline: Fla. oversight board sets Jan 3 deadline for Miami.

text.p: A state oversight board has given Miami until January 3 to approve a financial recovery plan, and city officials said Wednesday they hoped to beat the deadline.
Mayor Joe Carollo said he would set out a plan at Thursday's City Commission meeting, specifying how Miami could close its $68 million deficit.
Carollo previously told Reuters he thought that could be done without raising taxes or fees by selling or leasing valuable city-owned land.

Under the timetable set by the oversight board, Gov. Lawton Chiles would review and approve the city's recovery plan by Feb 1. The city, which is struggling to close the deficit in its $275 million budget for the year that began Oct 1, expects to run out of money in late February or early March unless changes are made.

Chiles declared Miami to have a fiscal crisis last week and appointed the five-member oversight board on Tuesday. Board members are acting as advisors, and have no authority to override the city commission.
